column4: A giant Awakened lobster (Homarus immanis) thriving in the PCB-enriched coastal waters of the North Sea. Grips prey in its claws and crushes it.

A crocodile-like dracoform (Crocodylus cymri) with a flat beaver-like tail, roughly 3 m plus a 1.5 m tail and ~375 kg of green-brown muscle. It digs, lives semi-socially, and ambushes large prey — sheep, cattle, even people — from the water.
A small dracoform — a flying serpent (Alutsewerpens lithuania) of Baltic folklore. Said to guard and protect its lair; extremely dangerous if cornered or threatened.
A large magical horse (Equus maximus) that can painfully dissolve into mist. Prized by horseflesh merchants; peaceful and benign unless abused.

The Celtic banshee (Spectris lamentaris) — a wailing death-spirit attached to a clan. Distinct from (and far more elaborate than) the system's generic Banshee. Dual-natured; at least one Tir Nan Og bean sidhe also casts manipulation spells.
A small, sly Awakened black cat (Felis nigra) that holds strong territorial ideas and toys with intruders using its mind-affecting powers. Sometimes kept as a (dangerous) pet.
column5: Woodland, heaths, rocky hills, fringes of urban areas

column4: The vengeful spirit of a woman burned in the witch trials (no accepted taxonomy). All Brocken bows have Essence Drain; roll 1D6 per other listed power — on a 1 that individual lacks it.

A vicious little Awakened stoat (Mustela stalini) used as a security animal. On a damaging bite it fastens to the wound, dealing escalating damage (7L, 8L, 9L…) on action 3 + 1D6 turns until killed or sated with blood.
column5: Woodland, hedgerows, grassland, rough grassland, moors

column4: A large Awakened beaver (Castor efforderis) that digs extensive tunnels and collapses them on intruders. Russian specimens are twice the size and ferocious enough to kill a bear one-on-one.
column5: In and around rivers and lakes, in wooded country

column4: A horse-bodied Awakened creature (Equus sagittarius); some are seen armed with polearms and armour near draco lairs.
A three-headed Awakened dog (Canis cerberi), impossible to surprise and often magically active. Blow off one head and it keeps coming.
column5: Rocky hills, plateaux, mountains, barren land

column4: A zombie — an animated corpse conditioned for simple labour or security. It never tires and feels no pain, but is slow and only semi-intelligent.
An Awakened macaque (Macaca cristatus) with a vicious temperament; some carry a horrible plague virus (Pestilence). Several escaped the Cordoba labs in 2051.
column5: Hills, barren lands, low mountain slopes

column4: A corrosive Awakened otter (Lutra ederis) of polluted waters, dissolving prey in acidic secretions. The old ones may possess shamanic talents.
column5: Polluted acidic rivers, lakes, canals (not sea water)

column4: A slow-moving venomous Awakened viper (Vipera pseudocanis aspis) that nests and ambushes lone wanderers. Its mimicry can act as a hypnotic song with a slight change of tone.
column5: Very varied, mountains to coast; prefers grasslands

column4: A man-eating water-horse of Scottish legend: it lures riders, then its highly adhesive skin traps them as it drags them under to drown and devour.
column5: Freshwater rivers, lochs, lakes, estuaries and fjords (seawater-tolerant)

column4: A stone-skinned winged gargoyle (Gargoyle saxsexus) that perches on tall derelict buildings. More dangerous the more it is injured.
A giant Norse wolf (Canis lupus aesir) of legend — fearsome, magically resistant, and most dangerous when wounded.
A jackal (Canis igni) that projects fire, gaining the ability at maturity. It uses decoy strategies rather than its flames to keep predators from its young.
column5: Steppe, scrub, low hills, outskirts of urban areas

column4: A savage giant of Irish myth (Homo foeditas) — a hulking, corrosive bog-dweller, often confused with trolls and the dzoo-noo-qua.
An Awakened polecat (Mustela putorius magnus) whose foul musk spray is harvested as an antipersonnel deterrent. The reek lingers for weeks and makes skin peel.
A giant Awakened biting fly (Culex pestilans). Females drain blood and Essence and carry a cyclical VITAS-related disease; males attack with mandibles.
column5: Marshes, swamps, heavily polluted and slow-moving freshwater

column4: A goblinized being (Homo bestius) created by a goblin-inducing HMHVV strain, spread directly from individual to individual. Drains Essence permanently.
An Awakened boar (Sus aureus) with golden tusks prized for enchanting — each male tusk is a unit of virgin telesma (two make a magical dagger).
A petrifying sea-dragon (Draco odiosus fabulosus). It walks up to a victim, petrifies them with its gaze, and pulls the head clean off.
A nearly-immortal, wise Awakened elk (Alces alces vetustus) — a gentle protector of its herd, with one deadly enemy in the fenrir wolf.
A multi-headed aquatic wyrm (Pleuracanthus polycaput) that develops a taste for flesh and savages anyone near its waters.
A majestic Awakened eagle (Aquila augustus) revered as a wise 'Old One' and medicine-lodge spirit; it senses approaching storms.
A giant Awakened dung/stag beetle (Lucanus fimus) breeding in sewers and polluted ground; its larvae lurk in warm city drains.
A Belgian shapeshifting spirit (no accepted taxonomy) with three forms — avian, canine, and feline. Dogs and cats always know it for what it is.
column5: Urban fringes, plains, grassland, light woodland

column4: A vast, wise Awakened whale (Megaptera palestrina) whose songs carry memory and meaning; it reincarnates alternately as male and female.
A magically-active Awakened falcon (Falco velox) that casts spells and works alongside the druids and bards of Wales, Scotland and Brittany.
column5: Grassland, hills, moorland; coasts in winter

column4: A small Swiss salamander (Salamandra exhaurius) that short-circuits magic: it drains the Force from spells cast near it and absorbs the energy to empower itself.
column5: Damp upland woods, Alpine springs, rivers

column4: A blind vampire variant (Sanguisuga europa caecus) that begins as an infected metahuman, keeping most of its attributes. Unlike the common vampire it can drain Essence permanently without limit.
A prophetic Awakened owl (Bubo ignavus maiusculus) reputed for precognition — its acute senses pick up faint seismic and pollutant cues before disaster strikes.
The winged horse of legend (Equus volatilis amplus), graceful and swift on the wing.
A winged stag (Cervus insolens) of ill omen, said to cast a man-shaped shadow.
A giant corrosive amoeba (Entamoeba imitatrix) that engulfs and digests prey, mimicking its victims' appearance. It oozes through moist ground and splits when it grows too large.
column5: Acidic lakes and rivers, marshes, swamps, any non-urban moist ground

column4: A lightning-fast Awakened mongoose (Herpestes illustris) and consummate snake-killer that dances its prey into a stupor before the kill.
A goat-legged Awakened creature (Capra satyrus) — a nimble climber fond of fermented fruit juice and bananas. (PAE critter, distinct from the Companion's satyr metahuman.)
A great Awakened albatross (Diomedea scintillans) of the northern seas whose scintillating plumage can dazzle and blind; at the equinox the males turn deadly.
A fire-immune Awakened scorpion (Euscorpius igneus) often conditioned as a security animal; it strikes with claws and a venomous sting.
column5: Wide range (prefers rocks, stones, brick walls, buildings)

column4: A large predatory Awakened pike (Esox sputare) that spits corrosive saliva at prey before closing to bite and engulf.
A tiny winged fairy (no accepted taxonomy) of Tir Nan Og, quick and elusive.
A magical toad (Bombina invisus) whose skin secretes acid when startled and a sebaceous hallucinogen when calm; its forebrain bone is prized for enchanting.
An aggressive, militant Awakened dolphin (Delphinus periculosis); its pods strike back hard at those who foul the seas.
A metal-feathered marsh bird (Ardea foedus) of Greek myth that launches its razor feathers like arrows.
column5: Marshes, swamps, estuaries, rivers, coastal waters

column4: A giant Awakened wolf spider (Lycosa saltator) whose venom sets victims dancing uncontrollably. Kept, improbably, as a pet.
column5: Wide range of damp land terrains

column4: A thrall (no accepted taxonomy) made when a vampire or nosferatu drains a victim's Essence to 0 and feeds it their blood. It keeps its former self's attributes and serves its master.
An Awakened porcupine (Hystrix sagittarius) that launches volleys of quills at attackers; a melee attacker risks getting stuck.
A savage bull-headed brute (Aurochs atrox) lurking in caves and tunnels; it is unaffected by all illusion spells.
A malevolent free spirit (Umbra metuculosus) born of violence, haunting the places where it died and driving the living to harm one another.
column5: Sites of violence, rural or urban

column4: A giant Awakened praying mantis (Mantis malus); the larger females are the dangerous ones, and insect shamans prize them.
A Slavic house-spirit (Anima mansuetas) — a free-willed brownie-like servant that adopts a rural household, guards it, and warns of danger. It fears cats and dogs.
A reclusive mining spirit (a knocker or rapper) that haunts mountains and mines, glamouring its territory and triggering 'accidental' rockfalls to drive off intruders.
column5: Inside mountains and hills, inside mines

column4: A spectral hound of the Wild Hunt — part of a ghostly host that rides the night sky. Travels (usually flying) over any terrain.
A fiery spectral steed of the Wild Hunt, carrying a ghostly huntsman across the sky and breathing flame.
A spectral huntsman of the Wild Hunt — one of the riders in the ghostly host.
The lead huntsman of the Wild Hunt — the most powerful member of the host, immune to illusion and able to bend the storm and the beasts to its will.
